sections.h2: Where is Larimer County, Colorado, and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Larimer County sits at the northern end of the Front Range, along the Wyoming border, and covers 2,634 square miles. Fort Collins is the county seat and its largest city. The 2020 census counted 359,066 residents.

Other communities include Loveland, Estes Park, Berthoud, Johnstown, Timnath, Wellington and Windsor, with Berthoud, Johnstown and Windsor reaching into Weld County. The county was created on November 1, 1861 and named for William Larimer, Jr., the founder of Denver.

Settlement here followed irrigation more than mining. Camp Collins grew into Fort Collins after an 1864 flood, the railroad came in 1877, sugar beets arrived in 1902 with a Great Western Sugar plant in Loveland, and the Colorado Big Thompson Project of the 1930s widened irrigated farmland. For owners, that history explains the mix of city lots, farm parcels and mountain cabins on one tax roll.

sections.h2: What does the Larimer County economy look like?
sections.html:
Colorado State University is the largest employer in Fort Collins, and the city also draws health care, public schools, government and manufacturing jobs. A 2024 city report listed these top Fort Collins employers.

Interstate 25 runs along the east side of Fort Collins, US 287 becomes College Avenue, and the MAX bus line serves the Mason Corridor. Denver International Airport is about 70 miles south.

sections.h2: Which Larimer County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor values property and takes protests. The Treasurer, who also serves as Public Trustee, mails statements and collects payment. Both offices are at 200 W. Oak Street in Fort Collins.

  • Treasurer and Public Trustee: Suite 2100, (970) 498-7020, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. Mailing address is P.O. Box 1250, Fort Collins, CO 80522.
  • Assessor: second floor, (970) 498-7050, same weekday hours. Mailing address is P.O. Box 1190.
  • Title companies can use the Treasury's CTD login, and mortgage servicers have a mass payment option.

The Treasurer states that it does not determine the amount of tax. Questions about value go to the Assessor, and the rate comes from the cities, county, schools and districts that tax your address.

sections.h2: How is a Larimer County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
The bill is assessed value times the mill levy, and assessed value is actual value times an assessment rate. For 2026 the county's guide lists residential rates of 6.8% for local government and 7.05% for schools, the first year residential property has two rates.

Step in the county's $275,000 exampleResult
Local government: $275,000 x 0.068, then x 0.023425$438.05
Schools: $275,000 x 0.0705, then x 0.052116$1,010.43
Total in the example$1,448.48

That example is a teaching figure from the county, not a quote for your house. Your own levy depends on every district on your bill. The county's guide to Colorado property taxes walks through the same math.

sections.h2: How does Larimer County value homes?
sections.html:
Real property is revalued in odd numbered years. Residential values for 2025 and 2026 rest on market conditions at June 30, 2024, using a 24 month sales study from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024. Vacant and commercial land uses 60 months of sales.

Two details matter to sellers. Foreclosure transfers to lenders are left out of the study, though resales of foreclosed homes are generally used. And the Assessor measures square footage from exterior dimensions, so a builder's interior figure may not match the county record.

Because 2026 is an intervening year, Notices of Valuation usually mail only when value or classification changed.

sections.h2: How do I protest a Larimer County valuation?
sections.html:
Protests are accepted from May 1 through June 8. You can file by mail, an online tool the county says takes 15 minutes or less, in person, by phone or appointment, by fax at 970-498-7070, or at the secure drop box at the southwest entrance of 200 W. Oak Street.

The county's 2026 assessor calendar sets the next steps: Notices of Determination by June 30, County Board of Equalization hearings from July 1 to August 5, and a July 15 deadline to appeal to that board. An alternate protest period runs later, with hearings from September 1 to November 2 and an appeal deadline of September 15.

You can only contest value or classification. Levies are set by the taxing districts, not by the Assessor.

sections.h2: What are the Larimer County payment options?
sections.html:
Taxes for 2025 were due in two equal installments, by the end of February and June 15, or in one payment by April 30. Partial payments are not accepted, and the county notes that amounts of $25 or less are due in full by April 30.

  • Pay online through the Treasury's payment system and print a receipt.
  • Sign up for eNotices and email reminders.
  • Use EquaPay for automated monthly payments if no mortgage escrow covers the taxes.
  • Ask about relief programs: senior exemption, veteran with a disability exemption, deferral, work off program, and the property tax, rent and heat rebate.

sections.h2: What happens at the Larimer County tax lien sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid real property taxes go to a public lien sale. The 2026 sale is scheduled for Thursday, November 19, 2026 at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch, 5280 Arena Circle, Loveland, with registration at 7:30 a.m. It is held in person, not online.

The 2026 investor rate is 13%, which state law sets as the federal discount rate on September 1 plus nine points. The advertising list is posted online in early October and updated nightly. Tax sale certificates cancel automatically after fifteen years.

The sale page did not state a redemption period, so ask the Treasurer for the timing on any lien against your house.

sections.h2: How do wildfire and flood history affect Larimer County sellers?
sections.html:
The Cameron Peak fire started August 13, 2020 in Roosevelt National Forest and was declared fully contained on December 2, 2020. It burned 208,663 acres and destroyed 469 structures, including 42 primary residences, and at one point reached within four miles of Loveland.

A Forest Service report cited in that account found that 36% of the burned land had high soil burn severity, with a high risk of erosion or flooding. Owners in Poudre Canyon, Red Feather Lakes, Redstone Canyon and Storm Mountain should expect buyers and insurers to ask about burn scar and defensible space.

Fort Collins itself has a cold semi-arid climate, with about 51 inches of snow and 16 inches of precipitation in an average year.

sections.h2: What do Larimer County sellers face with back taxes or an inherited house?
sections.html: The common problems are a delinquent bill, a title that needs a probate step, and a roof or foundation that makes a retail listing hard. A cash buyer can buy the house as it stands, but any tax lien still gets paid out of proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Treasurer at (970) 498-7020 first.

faqs.q: When are Larimer County property taxes due?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the first half was due February 28, the second half June 15 and a single full payment April 30. If a date falls on a non business day, it moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the Larimer County property tax protest deadline?
faqs.a: Protests to the Assessor are accepted May 1 through June 8. You can file by mail, online, in person, by phone or fax, or at the drop box at 200 W. Oak Street.

faqs.q: Does Larimer County run its tax lien sale online?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 sale is in person at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch in Loveland on November 19, 2026.

faqs.q: How are Larimer County homes valued for 2026?
faqs.a: 2026 is an intervening year, so residential values still reflect the June 30, 2024 appraisal date and a sales study from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

faqs.q: Who sets my Larimer County tax rate?
faqs.a: Taxing authorities such as cities, the county, school districts and fire districts set levies. The Assessor sets value and the Treasurer collects the bill.
